name: Vanuatu
snapshot: A Pacific nation rebuilding from a deadly December 2024 earthquake, which won a landmark advisory opinion on climate obligations from the International Court of Justice in 2025.
culture: Vanuatu has more than 100 languages, with Bislama as the national lingua franca. On Pentecost Island, men leap from tall towers with vines tied to their ankles in the land-diving ritual that inspired bungee jumping. Kastom, traditional custom, governs land and chiefly life. Kava is drunk in nakamals each evening.
society: Most people live from subsistence farming and fishing. Cyclones and earthquakes regularly strike. Vanuatu led the push for the ICJ's 2025 opinion that states have legal obligations to curb climate change. Its citizenship-by-investment programme lost EU visa-free access.
situation: After a snap election in January 2025, Jotham Napat became prime minister at the head of a coalition, ending a period of frequent no-confidence votes.
power: A parliamentary republic. Parliament elects the prime minister, and an electoral college chooses a largely ceremonial president; frequent no-confidence votes prompted reforms to curb party- switching.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Jotham Napat, since February 2025
